What comes up in Malabar

3 conditions, and each one is handled differently

Every site is scoped on the day. The table is what the work usually involves here rather than a statement about any particular property.

Small coastal block with constrained access

The standard Malabar job, where the method follows the access rather than the structure.

How it is handled
Smaller plant or hand work, with material carried out and loaded at the kerb in sequenced loads.
What does it
Mini excavator, hand tools, bogie or 10 wheeler tippers.

Weathered sheeting and outbuildings

Sheds, fencing and eaves that have been in the salt air for decades.

How it is handled
Condition assessed first, removed whole where possible and never broken up on site, then wrapped and taken to a licensed facility.
What does it
Licensed asbestos removalists, then a machine for the frame once clearance is issued.

Freestanding houses

Single and double storey brick, brick veneer, fibro and timber. The era matters more than the material, because anything built before 1990 carries a hazardous materials assumption until it is tested.

How it is handled
Hazardous materials removed and cleared first, services disconnected in writing, then the structure taken down and the material separated as it falls.
What does it
Excavator with a demolition grapple, sized to the side access rather than to the house. Zero tail swing where the work runs hard against a boundary.

Malabar

What shapes the work on these blocks

  • Heavy coastal exposure Older fibro and cement sheet weathers hard here, and its condition decides how it is handled.
  • Small older blocks With limited side access and neighbours close on both sides.
  • Narrow streets Where truck standing is arranged rather than assumed.
  • Steady knockdown rebuild activity On blocks that were originally modest and are now valuable.

Malabar streets are narrow and the blocks are small, so the question is usually what can stand at the kerb and what can reach the rear. A truck and dog is rarely an option, and the same volume goes out in more tipper loads as a result.

Malabar questions

What people ask before we start

The fibro is cracked and crumbling. Does that change anything?
Yes, potentially a great deal. Badly weathered or damaged cement sheet can have to be handled as friable, which means a higher licence class, full enclosure, air monitoring and a different clearance process.
Can you get a machine into the back yard?
It depends on the side gap and what is in it. Where nothing fits, the work goes to hand demolition with material carried out, and that is settled at the site visit rather than on the day.
There is no side access at all. Can the job still be done?
Usually, with a different method. Smaller plant, hand demolition where it is needed, and material carried out to the kerb rather than loaded where it falls. It is slower and it is priced that way.
Is Max licensed for the asbestos removal itself?
Max holds the demolition licence, AD214737. The asbestos removal is carried out by licensed asbestos removalists, and the air monitoring and clearance by an independent licensed assessor. The whole pathway is managed as one job so you are not coordinating three contractors.
